title: Anthem of the Independent Hills (Ka Sur Jingialeh Laitluid)
cultural_context: Solemn anthem from 'Ka Drama U Tirot Sing' sung by the Durbar of Chiefs affirming that native soil cannot be bartered or ceded to imperial foreign powers.

khasi: Kane ka ri dei ka ri ki blei,
Khlem da lah ban thied da ka spah;
Ki kpa tymmen ki la tei ia ka hima
Da ka bor jong ka nia bad ka hok;
To bat ia ka kti, ko ki myntri,
Wat aiti ia ka snieh-ri jong ngi;
Katba ka sngi ka dang tyngshain
Ngin ieng kum u mawsiang ba skhem.
english: This highland soil is the realm of the gods,
Never to be bought with foreign silver or gold;
Our ancestors established this sovereign state
By the strength of righteous reason and justice;
Clasp hands firmly, O noble ministers,
Never surrender our sacred native land;
As long as the sun illuminates the day,
We shall stand firm like immovable granite.

khasi: Lada ngi hap ha ka thma ba jur,
Ka nam jong ngi kan im junom;
Ki pateng kin kynmaw da ka burom
Ia kito kiba la aiti la ka mynsiem;
Ha Lum Diengiei bad Lum Shillong
Ka lyer kan rwai ia ka jingjop;
Ba u Khasi um ju mane mraw
Hynrei tang ia U Blei Uba Khraw.
english: Though we may fall in the fury of battle,
Our glorious name shall live forever;
Those who laid down their earthly lives;
Across Mount Diengiei and Shillong Peak
The mountain wind shall chant our victory:
That the Khasi bows to no earthly master,
Serving only the Supreme Almighty God.

vocabulary.snieh-ri: sacred soil / territory of the motherland
vocabulary.myntri: clan cabinet minister of the Khasi kingdom
